paragraphs.title: Elkanah’s Family and Their Journey to Shiloh

easy.explanation: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah.
easy.q: How many wives did Elkanah have?

answers: Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none
Hannah had children, but Peninnah had none
easy.explanation: The KJV says that Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.
easy.q: Who had children, and who had none?

easy.explanation: Elkanah went yearly to Shiloh to worship and sacrifice unto the Lord.
easy.q: Where did Elkanah go yearly to worship and sacrifice unto the Lord?

answers: Because Hannah was the eldest wife
medium.explanation: The KJV says, “he loved Hannah,” so he gave her a worthy portion.
medium.q: Why did Elkanah give Hannah a worthy portion?

answers: She helped Hannah travel to Shiloh
She provoked Hannah and made her fret
medium.explanation: Peninnah provoked Hannah sore and made her fret because Hannah had no children.
A worthy portion was a special or generous share given to Hannah.
medium.q: What does “a worthy portion” mean in this passage?

answers: Peninnah’s provocation and Hannah’s sorrow at having no children
challenge.explanation: Peninnah provoked Hannah, and Hannah was deeply distressed because she had no children.
challenge.q: What caused Hannah to weep and not eat?

answers: He did not know that she was sorrowful
He wanted to send her away
He tried to comfort her by expressing his love
challenge.explanation: Elkanah tried to comfort Hannah by assuring her of the value of his love.
challenge.q: What does Elkanah’s question about being better to Hannah than ten sons reveal?

answers: Going to Shiloh, receiving portions, Hannah being provoked, and Hannah weeping
Weeping, Samuel’s birth, and then the journey to Shiloh
Samuel being brought to Eli, followed by Peninnah’s provocation
challenge.explanation: The family went to Shiloh, portions were given, Peninnah provoked Hannah, and Hannah wept and did not eat.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is described in these verses?

easy.explanation: Hannah went to pray before the Lord at Shiloh.
Hannah asked the Lord for a man child.
easy.q: What did Hannah ask for in her prayer?

answers: That she was angry with him
easy.explanation: Because her lips moved but her voice was not heard, Eli thought she was drunken.
easy.q: What did Eli first think about Hannah?

answers: Give him unto the Lord all the days of his life
medium.explanation: Hannah vowed to give her son unto the Lord all the days of his life.
medium.q: What did Hannah vow to do if the Lord gave her a son?

medium.explanation: Hannah was suffering deep sorrow and distress.
medium.q: What does “bitterness of soul” mean in this passage?

answers: Her lips moved, but her voice was not heard
medium.explanation: Hannah prayed silently, so Eli saw her lips moving but could not hear her voice.
medium.q: Why did Eli mistakenly think Hannah was drunken?

answers: At first he accused her, but later he blessed her
At first he told her to pray, but later he became silent
At first he gave her a son, but later he took him away
challenge.explanation: Eli first thought Hannah was drunken, but after hearing her explanation he sent her away in peace.
challenge.q: What difference is shown between Eli’s first words and his later response?

answers: She began weeping and stopped eating
She went her way, ate, and was no longer sad
challenge.explanation: After Eli’s words, Hannah went her way, ate, and her countenance was no more sad.
challenge.q: What showed that Hannah’s condition changed after Eli spoke to her?

answers: As pouring out her soul before the Lord
challenge.explanation: Hannah said, “I have poured out my soul before the Lord.”
challenge.q: How did Hannah describe her prayer to Eli?

easy.explanation: They returned and came to their house at Ramah.
easy.q: Where did Elkanah and his household go after leaving Shiloh?

answers: She conceived and bare a son
She went alone to Shiloh again
easy.explanation: The KJV says that Hannah conceived and bare a son.

easy.q: What name did Hannah give her son?

answers: Because he was born at Shiloh
Because she had asked him of the Lord
Because it was his father’s name
medium.explanation: She said, “Because I have asked him of the Lord.”
medium.q: Why did Hannah call her son Samuel?

answers: Hannah asked for a son, and afterward she bore a son
Eli asked for a son for Hannah
Peninnah asked that Hannah have a son
medium.explanation: Hannah prayed for a child, and afterward the Lord remembered her and she bore Samuel.
medium.q: What connection is shown between Hannah’s prayer and Samuel’s birth?

answers: Elkanah and his household returned to their house
medium.explanation: The household returned to Ramah before Hannah conceived and bore Samuel.
medium.q: What happened before Samuel was born?

answers: He was given to her in response to her request to the Lord
He was born into Eli’s family
He was born during the journey to Shiloh
challenge.explanation: The name recalls that Hannah asked the Lord for him.
challenge.q: What does the name “Samuel” emphasize about Hannah’s relationship to the child?

answers: She went from having no children to becoming Samuel’s mother
She changed from Elkanah’s wife to Eli’s wife
She moved from Shiloh to Egypt
challenge.explanation: At the beginning Hannah had no children; here she has given birth to Samuel.
challenge.q: What change took place in Hannah’s life between the beginning of the chapter and these verses?

answers: The Lord had forgotten Hannah and refused to hear her
Hannah’s prayer and request were answered
challenge.explanation: The Lord remembered Hannah, and she conceived and bore the son she had requested.
challenge.q: What does “the Lord remembered her” indicate in the story?

paragraphs.title: Samuel Is Dedicated to the Lord

answers: She wanted to remain until the child was weaned
easy.explanation: Hannah said she would not go up until the child was weaned.
easy.q: Why did Hannah not go up with Elkanah at that time?

easy.explanation: Hannah planned to bring Samuel before the Lord after he was weaned.
easy.q: What would Hannah do after the child was weaned?

easy.explanation: Elkanah told her to do what seemed good and to tarry until the child was weaned.
easy.q: How did Elkanah respond to Hannah’s plan?

answers: Hannah brought Samuel, nursed him, and then gave birth
Hannah gave birth, nursed and cared for Samuel, and then planned to bring him to Shiloh
Elkanah brought Samuel, and Hannah took him back
medium.explanation: Hannah stayed home, gave her son suck until he was weaned, and then planned to bring him to the Lord.
medium.q: What order of events is described in these verses?

answers: Until the child learned to read
Until the child became an adult
medium.explanation: Hannah remained with Samuel until he finished nursing.
medium.q: What does “until the child be weaned” mean here?

answers: She prepared Samuel to be brought to the Lord after he was weaned
She decided to give Samuel to Peninnah
medium.explanation: Her stay was temporary and allowed her to bring Samuel to the Lord after he was weaned.
medium.q: How was Hannah’s decision to remain home related to her vow?

answers: He respected and supported her intention
He knew nothing about the vow
He tried to prevent her from keeping it
challenge.explanation: Elkanah supported Hannah and told her to do what seemed good.
challenge.q: What can be learned from Elkanah’s response to Hannah’s vow?

answers: Hannah planned to bring him after he was weaned
challenge.explanation: Hannah clearly said that she would bring Samuel before the Lord after he was weaned.
challenge.q: Why did delaying the journey to Shiloh not cancel Samuel’s dedication?

answers: At home he was nursed and raised, but later he would appear before the Lord
At home he was a priest, but later he would become a child
At home he was at Shiloh, but later he would return to Ramah
challenge.explanation: Samuel remained at home until he was weaned, and afterward he would be brought before the Lord.
challenge.q: What contrast is shown between Samuel’s life at home and his future purpose?

answers: To Shiloh, to the house of the Lord
easy.explanation: Hannah brought Samuel to the house of the Lord in Shiloh.
easy.q: Where did Hannah bring Samuel after he was weaned?

easy.explanation: Hannah brought the child to Eli.
easy.q: To whom did Hannah bring Samuel?

easy.explanation: Hannah said that the Lord had given her the petition she asked of him.
easy.q: What did Hannah say she had received from the Lord?

medium.explanation: She brought three bullocks, flour, and wine, along with Samuel.
medium.q: What did Hannah bring with Samuel to Shiloh?

answers: She dedicated Samuel to the Lord for all his life
She planned to lend him to Elkanah
She intended to take him home shortly
medium.explanation: Hannah declared that Samuel would be lent to the Lord as long as he lived.
medium.q: What does “I have lent him to the Lord” mean in Hannah’s declaration?

answers: To explain why she had brought Samuel
medium.explanation: Hannah explained that Samuel was the child for whom she had prayed.
medium.q: Why did Hannah remind Eli about her prayer?

answers: Because she received him in answer to prayer, she dedicated him to the Lord
Because she received him from Elkanah, she gave him to Peninnah
Because Eli requested him, she left him with Eli temporarily
challenge.explanation: The Lord answered Hannah’s prayer, so she gave Samuel to the Lord for all his days.
challenge.q: What connection did Hannah make between receiving the child and giving him to the Lord?

answers: Hannah prayed, Samuel was weaned, and then he was born
Samuel was weaned, brought to Shiloh, and Hannah explained her vow to Eli
Eli brought Samuel, and then Hannah prayed for him
challenge.explanation: After Samuel was weaned, Hannah brought him to Shiloh and explained her prayer and dedication to Eli.
challenge.q: Which sequence is correct at the end of the chapter?

challenge.explanation: Hannah said, “as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord.”
challenge.q: Short answer: How long was Samuel to be lent to the Lord?
